findings.title: Datetime in Celery task kwargs will fail JSON serialization
findings.body: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` now puts `assignment_source.to_dict()` into the kwargs of `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (assignment_source.py:27-28) returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` field as a `datetime` object. Celery serializes task kwargs, and Sentry's Celery configuration uses the JSON serializer, which cannot encode a `datetime`; enqueueing the task therefore raises an `EncodeError` ("Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable") for every outbound assignee sync. All previously passed kwargs were JSON-safe primitives (int/str/bool/None). The tests run tasks under `self.tasks()` (eager mode), which bypasses serialization, so this is not caught. Serialize `queued` as an ISO string/timestamp or drop it from the payload.

findings.title: `queued` default is bound once at import time instead of per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. Every source created without an explicit `queued` (including all `from_integration` calls) therefore reports the process start time rather than the time the assignment was queued. This is the classic mutable/static default pitfall and will produce wrong data for any future use of `queued` (e.g. latency or ordering). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets its own timestamp.

findings.title: Tests do not catch the shared `queued` default or payload serialization
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only asserts `result.get("queued") is not None`, so the module-level default (always non-None) passes even though every instance shares the same stale timestamp. Additionally, the outbound sync tests run under `self.tasks()` (eager), which skips Celery serialization, so nothing verifies that the `assignment_source_dict` task payload can actually cross the queue. Add a test asserting `queued` reflects construction time and a test that the produced dict is JSON-serializable / that `apply_async` succeeds without eager mode.

findings.title: New required-on-the-wire task kwarg breaks in-flight messages during a rolling deploy
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` gains a new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg, and callers now always send it (even when `None`). During a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new workers can be consumed by workers still running the previous `(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` signature, which will raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'`. The `@retry` decorator will retry these, but since the signature mismatch is not transient the retries are exhausted and the assignee syncs are dropped. Consider versioning the task or otherwise ensuring old consumers tolerate the new payload.
